sentences: Quantum space complexity asks what computations can be performed with a limited quantum workspace.
The cited paper characterizes unitary quantum space and relates quantum verification with exponentially small completeness–soundness gaps to classical space complexity.
Its closing questions ask what analogous characterizations hold when intermediate nonunitary operations are allowed.
Another direction is to understand quantum interactive proofs with exponentially small gaps, between better-understood precision regimes.
Progress would connect resource-bounded quantum computation to concrete matrix problems and clarify how measurement, interaction, and precision change its power.
